pull.title: mining: add getTotalFees(), protect m_block_template with mutex
pull.body:
This PR catches four birds with one stone:

- fixes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36515
- add a new `getTotalFees()` getter so IPC clients don't have to sum up individual transaction fees
- storing fees in `m_total_fees` simplifies the `WaitAndCreateNewBlock` implementation.
- make it easier to add fee info to (future) external templates, as requested in    https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35671#issuecomment-6065004542

The last commit contains the fix for #36515, which is made easier by the changes before it. It can be tested with: https://gist.github.com/Sjors/832841d705e62a6addaf8e6d4cf1b155 (the test itself didn't seem worth including, though I could look into simplifying it)

In case this PR doesn't make it, I'll open a fresh one with a direct fix.

> add a new getTotalFees() getter so IPC clients don't have to sum up individual transaction fees

I thought the client needed to access the individual fees, so we return a vector. It makes sense to return it so they don't have to sum them, so the vector one is now redundant? 


See minimal test that fails on our tsan functional tests.

+    def run_concurrent_template_access_test(self):

+        self.log.info("Running concurrent template access test")

+        async def async_routine():

+            reader_ctx, init = await make_capnp_init_ctx(self)

+                async def submit_loop():

+                        await template.submitSolution(
+                            writer_ctx, block.nVersion, block.nTime, block.nNonce, coinbase)
+                    done.set()
+
+                await asyncio.gather(read_loop(), submit_loop())
+                assert_equal(self.nodes[0].getblockcount(), height)

The vector was initially introduced for (internal) compatibility with the `getblocktemplate` RPC, which returns this fee information.

`sv2-tp` only uses fees (the total) for logging, the SRI implementation doesn't use it at all.

I haven't done an inventory of software out there that uses the fees from `getblocktemplate`. One use case I could imagine is a miner dashboard that shows the current template you're working on, and a breakdown of fees.

We definitely need the internal total. Providing the total and individual via IPC is trivial, so I think we should keep it.

> See minimal test that fails on our tsan functional tests.

It works and I'm open to taking it, but failure isn't deterministic (just very likely with the 100 iterations).
Concept ACK

> It works and I'm open to taking it, but failure isn't deterministic (just very likely with the 100 iterations).

Indeed, it is not deterministic but is sure to fail at some point.

ACK 4774cf1de6a4670323686bf93beb93035b3f6dad

This change fixes a data race between ipc calls running on different worker threads, where `submitSolution` modifies a template while another call reads it. It also adds the `getTotalFees` IPC method, allowing external clients to retrieve the total fees without summing individual transaction fees.

Ran @ismaelsadeeq’s ipc test with tsan, repeating each submission setting (100, 150, 200 and 300) 25 times. Without the mutex fix, every run detected the race. With the fix, every run passed with no race reports or timeouts

I think the test is worth including. even though reproduction depends on scheduling, it consistently caught the regression on my machine (macOS arm)

test: exercise concurrent IPC block template access

Read a template while submitting solutions through a separate IPC worker
thread to cover races between the getters and submitSolution(). Repeat
submissions to increase the chance of detecting a race under
ThreadSanitizer.

Bound the scenario and template cleanup using timeout_factor, and cancel
and await both concurrent tasks before destroying the template.

Co-authored-by: Abubakar Sadiq Ismail <48946461+ismaelsadeeq@users.noreply.github.com>

Might it be preferable to make `m_block_template` non-mutating? Do users of the interface even need the mutated template after submitting?
AFAICT no, so we could do that and make the template const, that way no race and we copy when mutating for submission.

> Might it be preferable to make m_block_template non-mutating? 

I think it's a preferable solution. With no writes after construction there's no race, and since `submitSolution()` already copies the block, calling `AddMerkleRootAndCoinbase()` on that copy instead of on the template costs nothing.

The documentation and tests would need to be updated too, since the in-place mutation is documented and tested since #33745 (released in v31).

The sv2-tp client apparently relies on that mutation (`SaveBlockAsync()`), but it may be easy to update.

> Do users of the interface even need the mutated template after submitting?

Yes. Both existing clients call `getBlock()` after submit to store a copy of the block. This is potentially very useful when debugging a rejected block.

> The sv2-tp client apparently relies on that mutation (`SaveBlockAsync()`), but it may be easy to update.

Clients could download the non-mutated block and re-apply the solution themselves before storing to disk. That's slightly more complicated, so I prefer the existing approach.
Could we just return the block copy after applying the solution?

@ismaelsadeeq in theory yes, but clients intentionally wait 1 second before requesting it. If the solution _is_ correct, we don't want to "distract" the node from relaying it and from producing the next template.

> If the solution is correct, we don't want to "distract" the node from relaying it and from producing the next template.

I don't understand what you mean here. Doesn't the new valid header get processed synchronously anyway?

A call to `getBlock()` locks `cs_main` (briefly). Since `sv2-tp` typically runs on the same machine, when it saves to disk it also blocks the OS. Creating the new template blocks `cs_main`. And IIUC so does our p2p code when it announces the new block and handles compact block missing-transaction requests.

That said, I haven't done a very thorough analysis on whether the 1 second delay before `getBlock()` actually matters.

> A call to getBlock() locks cs_main (briefly). Since sv2-tp typically runs on the same machine, when it saves to disk it also blocks the OS. Creating the new template blocks cs_main. And IIUC so does our p2p code when it announces the new block and handles compact block missing-transaction requests.

That should all be unrelated to copying a block. Or is the concern just that the OS might be something more important in the meantime and this might distract it? I don't think that is a valid concern.

I wrote:

> A call to `getBlock()` locks `cs_main` (briefly).

This is not the case.

I benchmarked the approach of making the template block immutable and returning the full block in `submitSolution()`. The good news is that there's no regression in compact block relay, not even when a transaction is missing.

But it does add a 6ms slowdown to when sv2-tp serves the next template. That's because IPC code still bottlenecks a few things on a single thread (even with multiple connections).

I was able to reduce that by having sv2-tp skip block deserialization (including sha256 hashing), and write the serialized bytes straight to disk (after a 500ms delay). That still left 2.5ms.

Things can be sped up further by:
1. having another thread copy the result (1ms) 
2. taking advantage of Capnp shared memory support: https://capnproto.org/cxxrpc.html (1ms)
3. more fundamentally making IPC (response) handling parallel

These require changes to libmultiprocess.

So my preference would be to defer making CBlockTemplate const until after these improvements land. This would be a breaking change for clients, but that's straight-forward to work around.
